name: ZeroAvia
blurb: Develops hydrogen-electric powertrains for commercial aviation. ZA600 system (660kW) targeting 2026 entry-into-service for 9-19 seat aircraft. Backed by Alaska Airlines, United Airlines, and IAG.

name: Airbus ZEROe
blurb: Airbus program developing a hydrogen fuel cell-powered commercial aircraft targeting mid-2030s entry into service. Selected fuel cells over combustion in 2025 after extensive testing of both technologies.

name: H2FLY
blurb: Subsidiary of Joby Aviation. Achieved world's first piloted liquid hydrogen-powered electric aircraft flight in 2023. Developing modular fuel cell systems from 30kW to 2MW for regional aircraft.

name: Cranfield Aerospace Solutions
blurb: UK-based developer of hydrogen-electric conversion kits for small regional aircraft. Working with Air New Zealand, EVIA AERO, and MONTE Aircraft Leasing. Collaborating with Safran on 50-PAX regional aircraft.

name: Beyond Aero
blurb: Developing hydrogen-powered business jets for private and corporate aviation. Focused on light jets using hydrogen propulsion technology for zero-emission private travel.

name: Stralis Aircraft
blurb: Australian company developing hydrogen-electric propulsion systems for commercial aircraft, drones, and vehicles. Targeting regional aviation markets across Asia-Pacific.

name: Universal Hydrogen
blurb: Pioneer in hydrogen logistics and aircraft conversion kits for regional turboprops. Raised $82.5M from GE Aviation, American Airlines, Airbus, JetBlue, and Toyota. Operations wound down in 2023.

name: GKN Aerospace (H2 GEAR)
blurb: GKN Aerospace's H2 GEAR project has successfully ground-tested a cryogenic fuel cell powertrain demonstrating megawatt-scale hydrogen propulsion for regional aircraft.

name: Rolls-Royce
blurb: Running hydrogen ground tests on gas turbines for sustainable aviation. Partnered with EasyJet to accelerate hydrogen-powered engine development. Exploring combustion-based hydrogen propulsion for larger aircraft.

name: CFM International
blurb: Joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran. Modifying GE Passport turbofan for hydrogen combustion testing. Working with Airbus on A380 demonstrator flight program.

name: Destinus
blurb: Developing hypersonic hydrogen-powered aircraft for long-distance cargo and passenger transport. Targeting speeds of Mach 5+ with liquid hydrogen combustion propulsion.

name: Joby Aviation
blurb: eVTOL leader and parent of H2FLY. Successfully flew a hydrogen-powered VTOL aircraft 523 miles — believed to be the first forward flight of a VTOL powered by liquid hydrogen.

name: United Therapeutics (UT H2eR44)
blurb: Made the first piloted hydrogen fuel cell-powered eVTOL flight in March 2025 using a modified Robinson R44 helicopter in Québec. Targeting 200nm range with 500lb payload.

name: Aalto HAPS (Zephyr)
blurb: Airbus-backed spin-off operating the Zephyr solar-powered fixed-wing HAPS. Set a 67-day endurance record in 2025. Preparing commercial demonstration over Japan in 2026 with NTT Docomo. One of only two companies to have flown HAPS through day and night.

name: SoftBank (HAPSMobile / Sunglider)
blurb: Developed the 78-meter wingspan Sunglider solar-electric HAPS. Planning commercial stratospheric service launch in Japan by late 2026 for rural broadband and 5G connectivity.

name: Skydweller Aero
blurb: US-Spanish aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft for perpetual flight. Based on record-breaking Solar Impulse technology. HQ in Oklahoma City with R&D in Spain and Mississippi. Partnered with Thales in 2025 for long-endurance surveillance.

name: BAE Systems (PHASA-35)
blurb: PHASA-35 completed successful stratospheric test flights in December 2024 reaching 66,000 feet. Showcasing rapid reusability and enhanced payload for defense and surveillance. Targeting operational readiness by 2026.

name: Sceye
blurb: U.S.-based HAPS company flying stratospheric airship platforms. One of only two companies that has flown HAPS through both day and night. Active in commercial pilots for disaster resilience and emergency communications.

name: Thales Alenia Space (Stratobus)
blurb: Developing Stratobus, a semi-rigid stratospheric airship for persistent surveillance, disaster monitoring, and sovereign communications. Positioning for hybrid space-terrestrial-HAPS network architectures.

name: Stratospheric Platforms Ltd
blurb: Cambridge startup designing a 60-meter-wingspan HAPS platform powered by hydrogen fuel cells to avoid solar day-night cycle limitations. One of the few HAPS developers pursuing hydrogen propulsion.

name: AeroVironment
blurb: Defense-focused HAPS developer. Horus A certification demonstrates clear commercialization pathway. Long-standing partner with NASA and USGS. North America's leading HAPS operator for defense ISR missions.

name: Aerostar (Raven HAPS)
blurb: Stratospheric balloon-based HAPS operator, spin-off from Raven Industries. Regularly flying HAPS test missions in the stratosphere. Active in commercial and defense connectivity and surveillance applications.

name: Near Space Labs
blurb: Sells change detection imagery from stratospheric balloon platforms to insurance providers. Focused on commercial earth observation applications from near-space altitude.

name: Prismatic (PHASA-35 heritage)
blurb: Developer with PHASA-35 heritage exploring advanced meteorology for HAPS tropospheric ascent and descent. Operating from Spaceport America with stratospheric flight achievements in 2023. Targeting PHASA operations from 2028.
